family_tax_benefit_note.meaning: Descriptive note on Family Tax Benefit Part A and Part B (no rate table).

value.summary: Family Tax Benefit (FTB) is a 2 part payment that helps with the cost of raising children. To get it you must have a dependent child aged 15 or younger (or a full-time secondary student aged 16 to 19 not getting a pension, payment or benefit like Youth Allowance), care for the child at least 35% of the time, and meet an income test. The payment is worked out using the FTB rate and income test for the current financial year (1 July to 30 June) and is balanced against actual income after the year ends. Rates and income-test limits are set per financial year from 1 July; the pages read do not themselves use the word indexed.
value.parts: FTB Part A is paid per eligible child: a base rate and a higher maximum rate that depends on the child age, reduced by an income test on adjusted taxable income and affected by the number and ages of children, percentage of care and child support; an annual FTB Part A supplement is paid after balancing. FTB Part B is paid per family, mainly for single parents or carers and some couples, with maximum rate depending on the age of the youngest child (0 to 4, or 5 to 18); partnered families face a 2 part income test (primary earner limit, then secondary earner income); an annual FTB Part B supplement is paid after balancing.
